summary.intent: Make the npm version bump in callisto-manifests edit package.json in place, preserving hand-formatted layout, line endings, BOM and dependency ranges, instead of reserializing the whole file.
summary.outcome: Added a json_text module for in-place JSON edits, wired it into npm.rs persist with a fallback and a shared atomic write_text, and added property and manifest-level tests. Updated the versioning spec and AGENTS.md, added a changeset, ran full CI, and shipped a PR. The real-world smoke diff is now exactly one line.

repo: callisto-manifests npm persist keeps the original text and parsed document at open, then tries an in-place edit at persist and falls back to full reserialization.
Both persist paths go through a single write_text that adds the byte order mark, writes atomically, and refreshes the remembered source.
AGENTS.md invariant 2 and docs/specs/versioning.json rewrite criteria describe JSON layout behavior and must be updated when the rewrite behavior changes.
The repo's full CI includes clippy, which flags redundant closures in test generators.
Work is done in a git worktree at .claude/worktrees/smoke-main, and the npm tests live in a separate npm/tests.rs file.
Changes to behavior need a changeset in addition to the code and spec updates.

code.finding: New module for in-place JSON text edits. Property test checks parse equality and surrounding length instead of fragile prefix/suffix assertions.
Opens with the original text and document retained, tries the in-place edit at persist, and routes all writes through write_text.
Added behavior tests for layout, line endings, BOM, dependency ranges and the fallback path.

workflow: Use a real-world smoke script, such as an npm format diff over a hand-formatted package.json, to verify that the change gives a minimal diff.
Prefer property-style assertions that pin the invariant (parse equality, length) over brittle exact-string assertions.
Run the full CI, including clippy, before shipping the PR, and rerun it after lint fixes.

friction: An edit to npm/tests.rs was refused because the file had changed since the last read, so the region had to be re-read and located again.
Clippy flagged a redundant closure in the new test generator, requiring a lint fix and a full CI rerun.
One prefix/suffix assertion in the property test was fragile and had to be simplified.
